summary: Concordia Venus is a card-driven economic game about building trade networks across the Roman map, using a hand of role cards that get better as you buy more of them. It's calm and cerebral, with victory hinging on a hidden multiplier formula few players see coming until the reveal.
criticised: scoring formula (Prefects/multipliers) is hard to plan around for newcomers
can feel a bit dry or thinky for non-Euro fans
map choice greatly affects strategy leading to snowbally openings
some find the theme thin dressing on a mechanism

interaction.detail: Colonists settle into shared cities on a common map, and each city's limited capacity means settling early can block rivals from that spot. Players also bid against each other in a shared Dutch-auction market for the same deck of personae cards, though resource production and hand-building remain private.

subsystems: colonist/production network scoring (goods types × colonist count)
personal bonus-card scoring (e.g. Vesta, Jupiter, Saturnus, Mercury)
scoring.how_you_win: Players place colonists to produce and trade goods, replaying cards from a growing personal deck; once someone plays their last card of the triggering type the round finishes, and points are tallied for colonists per good type plus a chosen bonus card, highest total wins.
